sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ECC is a large collection of agents, skills, hooks and rules that turns an AI coding agent into a more structured engineering system. It makes the agent plan, test, implement, review, verify and remember what worked.
sixtySeconds.problem: Getting a coding agent to work carefully usually means re-explaining your process in every prompt. ECC installs that process once: 72 agents, 328 skills, hooks, memory and security scanning, per the README.
whoFor: Claude Code users who want a ready-made engineering setup
Codex, Qoder and Kimi Code users
Developers who want security scanning of agent config (AgentShield)
Teams standardising how agents plan and review
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want a big, maintained toolbox you can install in one step and trim by profile. If you prefer a small, focused workflow, a lighter skills pack may suit you better.
requirements: Claude Code 2.1 or newer on PATH for the Claude plugin path

overview: ECC gives your coding agent a loop of plan, test, implement, review, verify, remember and improve. It ships specialised agents for planning, review, build repair, security and architecture, plus skills for TDD, research, docs, frontend, data, ML and operations.

It works best with Claude Code, has native plugin paths for Codex and Qoder, and adapters with fewer capabilities for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, GitHub Copilot and others. Hooks add enforcement, session summaries and continuous learning, and AgentShield scans prompts, hooks, MCP config, permissions and secrets.
The open-source repository is MIT licensed. ECC Pro is a separate paid GitHub App for private repos. The README warns to install only from the official GitHub repository and npm packages.

troubleshooting.problem: ECC appears twice or hooks fire twice
troubleshooting.solution: Usually caused by installing the plugin and then a full manual install on top. Remove the plugin, run node scripts/ecc.js uninstall --dry-run, then reinstall using one path.
Don't add a hooks field to .claude-plugin/plugin.json; Claude Code 2.1+ loads hooks/hooks.json automatically.

troubleshooting.problem: npm reports a version or cache error
troubleshooting.solution: Check the published version with npm view ecc-universal version before retrying.
